stemBlocks.value: Using a ruler, a pencil and a pair of compasses: (i) Construct accurately the square ABCD with sides 6 cm.
Think first: One accurately constructed right angle is all a square needs — the rest is equal arcs of 6 cm.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p158-q15 from workbook page 158.

solutionSteps.instruction: Draw a base line and mark AB = 6 cm.
Construct a perpendicular to AB at A.

contentBlocks.value: Arcs of equal radius each side of A on the line, then equal larger arcs from those two points crossing above A

solutionSteps.instruction: Mark D on the perpendicular with AD = 6 cm.

contentBlocks.value: Compasses set to 6 cm, centre A

solutionSteps.instruction: Draw arcs of radius 6 cm from B and from D; call the crossing point C.
Join BC and DC, then check the figure.

contentBlocks.value: All four sides 6 cm; each diagonal should measure 6√2 ≈ 8.5 cm

strategyBlocks.value: Draw AB = 6 cm, construct a perpendicular at A, mark D 6 cm along it, then cut arcs of radius 6 cm from B and D to locate C.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) A square ABCD with all four sides 6 cm and all angles 90°. Accuracy check: each diagonal measures 6√2 ≈ 8.5 cm.

whyThisWorks.value: A quadrilateral with four equal sides and one right angle must be a square: the equal arcs guarantee the rhombus, and the constructed perpendicular upgrades it to a square. Because the construction uses only compasses and a straight edge, the right angle is exact rather than eyeballed.

commonErrors.misconception: Using a protractor or set square instead of compasses.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using a protractor or set square instead of compasses.

commonErrors.misconception: Setting the compasses to slightly different radii for the two 6 cm arcs, so C is off.

commonErrors.misconception: Erasing construction arcs before the work is marked.

examTip.value: Keep the compasses locked at 6 cm for every side arc — reopening them mid-construction is the commonest source of a lopsided square.
